text: Gold finished Friday about flat near $3,883 (up $7 on the day) but posted a steep weekly loss as Treasury yields rose and Fed hike bets held.
Silver fell about 2.6% to near $48.60, its lowest in about a year, so the gold/silver ratio jumped to about 79.9; SLV fell 2.2% to $44.13, and AGQ trades on silver.
The miners held up better than metals: GDX slipped 0.24% to $81.64 and GDXJ about 0.6%; GDXU tracks GDX at three times the move.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.15% after producer prices showed inflation still running hot (6.5% a year).
Tech led stocks lower as Nvidia's leadership change kept weighing on chip stocks: Nasdaq −0.91%, S&P 500 −0.4%, QQQ −1.2% to $679.89; this matters for TQQQ and SQQQ.
USD/JPY briefly topped 160 for the first time since September before closing near 159.84, and the dollar index rose to about 103.4.
Brent settled nearly unchanged at $95.84, its second weekly loss in a row on signs of a supply surplus; this matters for NRGU.
Bitcoin slid further to about $68,400, below $69,000 for the first time since August.
